alternatives.argument: The local definition fixes the Euclidean dilation convention, derives the regular-function formula by change of variables, defines convergence test by test, and then defines scaling degree as the threshold infimum. It also defines extension, degree of divergence, and exact homogeneity. These clauses fully cover the harvested definition without relying on the unstamped PDF.

The complete local proof uses the dyadic partition f(2^j x), subtracts the Taylor jet through floor(delta-n) when delta>=n, and proves absolute convergence and continuity with the uniform annular-order lemma. The moving-scale estimate splits fine shells lambda<=C rho, intermediate coarse shells C rho<lambda<=lambda0, and finitely many outer shells; geometric sums give rho^-omega for delta<omega<min(Omega,n+k+1). Restriction gives the matching lower bound, so the extension has exactly degree delta. The source itself refers to Brunetti-Fredenhagen for its proof.

The complete local proof subtracts two same-degree extensions, uses the point-support theorem to write the difference as a finite delta jet, and tests its top nonzero order with a cutoff monomial to prove scaling degree n+m. The degree bound forces m<=floor(delta-n), excluding every nonzero jet below n; conversely each listed jet preserves degree delta by the extension theorem and restriction lower bound.

The complete local proof establishes the cutoff-subtracted functional is continuous, computes sigma(S^3)=2 pi^2 from the Gaussian integral and polar coordinates, differentiates the absolutely integrable cutoff difference in log(mu), and obtains the exact coefficient 1/(8 pi^2). Dilation gives rho^4(T_mu)_rho=T_mu+(8 pi^2)^-1 log(rho) delta_0; the finite-jet classification then excludes a homogeneous same-degree extension. This exact Euclidean calculation is additional to the source, which only supplies the general scaling-degree context.
